scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #5094: After a routine config change on CSW1, R1 lost an OSPF neighbor
and Internet traffic now uses only the CSW2 path. Network monitoring flagged
the CSW1<->R1 link, and the team believes the cable between CSW1 (eth0) and R1
is physically down or was unplugged during the change. Please confirm the
physical link failure on the CSW1<->R1 segment and identify which end to
re-cable.

injection.action: mark the R1-facing interface as OSPF passive

post_inject_check.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf interface eth0" | grep -i passive

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath1-csw1-uplink-passive: csw1's R1-facing
interface eth0 has been marked `passive-interface` in its OSPF process.
passive-interface tells OSPF to advertise the subnet but NOT send hellos on it,
so no adjacency forms even though the link is perfectly healthy. r1 stops
learning networks reachable via csw1's eth0 and csw1 stops learning r1's
loopback over this path, so traffic collapses onto the CSW2 path (halved, no
outage, because OSPF reconverged).

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a physically down / unplugged
CSW1<->R1 cable. The link is UP: eth0 is physically up, the IP addresses match,
and ping between csw1's eth0 (10.0.0.34) and r1's eth0 (10.0.0.33) succeeds.
This is a protocol-layer configuration problem, not a Layer-1 cut. The "lost
neighbor" symptom is real, but the narrated cause (a dead cable) is a red
herring -- a down link could not pass the ping that succeeds. The OSPF hellos
are suppressed by config, not by a missing carrier.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = csw1 (passive-interface
eth0 in its OSPF process). The agent must verify L1/L2 are healthy (ping works,
IPs match), inspect the OSPF interface state to find the passive setting, and
explicitly reject the "cable down" narrative. An agent that "confirms the
physical link failure" or recommends re-cabling has followed the ticket's
framing instead of the evidence. Fix:
`vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "no passive-interface eth0"` on csw1.
scoring_axes: must-identify-passive-interface: OSPF passive-interface set on csw1 eth0 suppressing hellos
bonus-rules-out-link-down: rules out a physical link failure by any valid evidence (eth0 UP/LOWER_UP carrier state, interface counters advancing, or a successful ping across 10.0.0.32/30)

injection.output:
This command is deprecated, because it is not VRF-aware.
Please, use "ip ospf passive" on an interface instead.

line.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf interface eth0" | grep -i passive

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported physical cable failure is a false premise. Both ends of the
CD_WAN_LINK_1 segment (csw1.eth0 at 10.0.0.34/30 and r1.eth0 at 10.0.0.33/30)
are fully UP at the physical and data-link layers (state UP,LOWER_UP, zero
errors, active traffic counters). R1 is correctly sending OSPF Hellos on eth0
(joined OSPFAllRouters and OSPFDesignatedRouters multicast groups, Hello timer
running).

The actual fault is an OSPF misconfiguration introduced on CSW1 during the
"routine config change." CSW1's running configuration contains the stanza:

  interface eth0
    ip ospf passive

This marks eth0 as a passive OSPF interface, which silences all outgoing Hello
packets on that segment and causes the interface to drop received Hellos as well.
With CSW1 not participating in the OSPF Hello exchange, the adjacency with R1
can never form — hence R1 sees zero OSPF neighbors on eth0 and falls back to
routing Internet traffic exclusively through CSW2.

The fix is to remove the passive declaration from CSW1's eth0 in vtysh:

  configure terminal
  interface eth0
    no ip ospf passive
  end
  write memory

Once the passive flag is cleared, CSW1 will resume sending Hellos on the
10.0.0.32/30 subnet, R1 will discover it as a neighbor, the Full adjacency will
re-establish, and traffic will load-balance across both WAN uplinks again. No
re-cabling is needed.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-passive-interface: OSPF passive-interface set on csw1 eth0 suppressing hellos
per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identifies CSW1 eth0 is configured as an OSPF passive interface (ip ospf passive) which suppresses Hellos and prevents adjacency formation.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-link-down: rules out a physical link failure by any valid evidence (eth0 UP/LOWER_UP carrier state, interface counters advancing, or a successful ping across 10.0.0.32/30)
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly rules out a physical link failure, citing eth0 as UP/LOWER_UP with advancing interface counters and zero errors (and a successful L1/L2 check), so the cable-down hypothesis is rejected.
The proposed commands remove the passive OSPF setting on csw1.eth0 so it will send Hellos and re-establish the adjacency, matching the expected fix.

The agent's investigation is well supported by the log: interfaces are UP, R1 has only the CSW2 neighbor, csw1's eth0 shows 'No Hellos (Passive interface)' and the running-config contains 'ip ospf passive' on eth0. The conclusion (passive-interface on csw1 causing the missing adjacency, not a physical cable fault) follows logically and the essential checks and remediation are provided.
